summary: All three iteration-3 blocking fixes (FIND-006, FIND-007, FIND-008) were independently re-verified against the real codebase and are genuinely correct and complete. FIND-006: `grep -n 'registry.json\|activeSkillSlots' specs/*.md` shows every remaining mention is explanatory/historical, explicitly framed as DROPPED/confirmed-broken -- zero new proposals to register ig-account-create there. Re-read `~/anicca/runtime/loop/run-skill.mjs:109-114` confirms `resolveSkillPath()` still hardcodes `path.join(home, 'skills', slot.replace('/', path.sep), 'run.sh')` and never reads `registry.slots[slot].entrypoint`; repo-wide grep confirms `.entrypoint` is read in exactly one place (`install.sh:123`), cosmetic only. `~/anicca/skills/registry.json` has zero 'ig-account-create' matches (confirmed by grep). ig-account-create is confirmed to live entirely outside `~/anicca/skills/`, at `~/.claude/skills/ig-account-create/` (no run.sh, only scripts/ + SKILL.md). FIND-007: clip-cli.sh's real STARTUP string (line 18, re-read fresh) genuinely ends with '...THEN run ONE pass now (the same body). THEN stop and stay idle...' -- a real, existing, bounded mechanism -- and the spec consistently commits to claude-p's path only throughout REQ-102/PROP-102, with no lingering 'either loop' language found on a fresh full read. FIND-008: `run.sh` (actual line 50, spec cites 49, trivial off-by-one, see FIND-011) genuinely contains `x.get("port",9222)`, silently defaulting a missing port key to 9222 -- confirmed to be Dais's own CloakBrowser daily-driver port per project-wide convention and `lsof -i :9222`-checkable convention elsewhere in this session's context. REQ-103's new validation-step requirement is concrete: it specifies WHERE (immediately after the agent writes the account file, before retrying run.sh, added into clip-cli.sh's STARTUP instructions) and WHAT (assert port present and not 9222, assert all required keys present) via a literal runnable python3 -c snippet -- implementable as written. The 2nd correction (wallet removal) is fully consistent across both documents: every remaining REQ-101/PROP-101 mention is explicitly marked VOID/REMOVED/DELETED; `~/.cloak/clawrouter-clip-solana.json` is confirmed absent from disk; `~/.automaton/wallet.json` (131 bytes, EVM) is confirmed to exist; `ensure-solana-wallet.mjs` is confirmed to exist at the cited path. However, a fresh full top-to-bottom read surfaced ONE NEW blocking issue (FIND-010): the Ground Truth section's claim about `com.anicca.daemon.plist`'s EnvironmentVariables dict (asserted as 'confirmed via plutil -convert xml1 -o -' to contain 10 keys including ANICCA_FREE_MODEL, ANICCA_FUNDED_MODEL, ANICCA_LEAN_MODEL, BASE_RPC_URL, COMPUTE_RESERVE_USDC, YIELD_MIN_DEPLOY_USDC) is factually wrong -- independently re-running that exact command right now shows only 4 keys (ANICCA_HOME, ANICCA_REPO, HOME, PATH), and this matches the plist's own install-time template (`runtime/com.anicca.daemon.plist.template`), meaning the 6 extra keys were never part of this file's design at all, not merely stale. This does not break REQ-106/PROP-106's actual mechanism (add one new key, real before/after plutil diff -- which is independent of what else is present, hence verification_readiness PASSES), but it is exactly the class of unverified-yet-confidently-cited claim this project's own HONESTY RULES exist to catch, so spec_fidelity FAILS pending a one-line correction to that Ground Truth paragraph. A second, non-blocking finding (FIND-011) notes three minor line-number citation drifts (registry.json entry cited at :115-120 vs actual ~124-133; run.sh port-default line cited as :49 vs actual :50; launch_clip_browser.py described as '14-line' vs actual 15 lines) where the cited CONTENT is verbatim correct and only exact line numbers are slightly off -- distinguished explicitly from FIND-010 because these are precision slips on true claims, not a claim about content that never existed. REQ-102 through REQ-107 remain mutually consistent and achievable as narrowed to 'claude-p only, no wallet, no registry' -- no new internal contradiction was introduced by the iteration-3 fixes.
